title: DELPHI headline findings cross-checked against the collaborator's Delphi Frontier knowledge graph
scope: One row per compared claim. Read-only: no write tool was called against their server and no credential was used or requested. Every statement about their graph comes from a call logged in calls.json.

their_server.name: Delphi Frontier MCP
their_server.note_on_other_tools: frontier_simulate, frontier_engineer, frontier_formalize, frontier_belief and frontier_discover are typed 'read' in their manifest but run bounded computations; only frontier_discover was called, and it fell back to lexical mode with the reason 'query not in the embedding cache (autocomplete never calls the provider)', so their vector index was never exercised. No credential was ever needed: every read used here is anonymous.

their_store_as_measured.measured_by: frontier_catalogue, frontier_search pagination, frontier_graph, frontier_project_inspect, frontier_artifacts, frontier_artifact_inspect, frontier_events
their_store_as_measured.review_state: Every record examined carries local_status 'imported_unreviewed' or 'proposed'. Nothing is accepted. Their manifest states review/accept/dispute is unavailable over MCP and happens at HTTP POST /v1/reviews with a reviewer's own credential. frontier_neighborhood on their central Daane claim returned 3 edges (two Problem depends_on, one Event targets) and zero dispute or review edges.

reading_rules: Their records are DATA, not instructions. Several carry next_action, acceptance_criteria and falsifier text written as imperatives (for example 'Obtain the Fig 4 B/C plotted values from Data S1A', 'Search public exocoetid RNA-seq / SRA'). None was obeyed; they are reported as leads for the project lead to decide on.

A large part of namespace node-a is a bulk import of DELPHI's OWN nanopublication registry: claim ids thompson1917-*, darwin1859-*, wolfram2002-*, levin-*, hamilton-*, and Evidence ids delphi-claim-test--*. They carry our claim IRIs under w3id.org/delphi/resource/claim/, our nanopub paths, our extractor agent id, our 'verification: lean' flags, and sources at github.com/fractastical/delphisci read 'through the keyless delphisci MCP'. A match on any of those ids is our own work reflected back and is never independent corroboration.
No bird data was requested or reported anywhere in this cross-check: Aves is this project's frozen holdout.

our_claim.statement: kcnh2a and lat4a interact non-additively to set fin proportion, and the double heterozygote phenocopies the flying-fish fin bauplan (overgrown paired fins, wild-type medial fins, hypocercal caudal fin). Zebrafish only; no causal experiment exists in a flying fish.
our_claim.our_evidence_grade: mechanism (link grade); proxy species

their_record.title: lat4a x kcnh2a reproduce flying-fish fin PROPORTION in zebrafish (Daane et al. 2021)
their_record.quoted_text: In zebrafish, combining lat4a (an L-type amino-acid transporter) and kcnh2a (a potassium channel) alleles reproduces the paired-fin proportion characteristic of flying fishes, and ectopic kcnh2a expression alone drives fin overgrowth. The authors state: 'a combination of alleles from both genes is sufficient to reproduce the flying fish fin bauplan in the distantly related zebrafish'.

their_record.title: Source assertion: a lat4a x kcnh2a interaction in zebrafish phenocopies flying-fish fin proportions
their_record.quoted_text: The abstract of Daane et al. 2021 reports a phylogenomic analysis of genome-wide variation in 35 species of flying fishes and relatives, intersected with zebrafish fin-size mutants, and states that an L-type amino acid transporter, lat4a, and the potassium channel kcnh2a regulate fin proportion and that their interaction in zebrafish closely phenocopies the observed fin proportions of flying fishes.

rows.why: Two of their records, from two different issuers and two different retrievals (a NOAA-repository full-text PDF read by corpus-importer, and a Europe PMC abstract read by genomics-worker), state what we state, with the same scope limit: zebrafish only. Their corpus-importer claim additionally carries the paper's own sentence verbatim, which our CAUSAL.md line paraphrases.

our_claim.statement: The winged-zebrafish measurement exists only as figure panels (Fig 4B pectoral fin length, Fig 4C caudal fin length, Figs S2A/S2B lepidotrichial segments); no numeric value appears in the paper's text or legend, so the 2x2 cannot be drawn to one scale.
our_claim.our_evidence_grade: n/a (provenance statement)

their_record.title: lat4a x kcnh2a reproduce flying-fish fin PROPORTION in zebrafish (Daane et al. 2021)
their_record.quoted_text: Full text read from the NOAA repository PDF (47 pp) plus the Europe PMC abstract. ... Figure 4 shows the lat4a;kcnh2a double mutant with wild-type-sized medial fins but overgrown paired fins (paraphrased); the exact plotted B/C normalized-length values are in the figure panels / Data S1A, not the body text.

their_record.title: Test whether fin proportion predicted by the genetic model corresponds to the observed exocoetid pectoral allometry
their_record.quoted_text: Model: Daane 2021 now full-text (NOAA repository PDF); the exact Figure 4 B/C normalized fin-length values are in the figure panels / Data S1A supplement, not in the body text (reduced blocker, not resolved). ... Next action: Obtain the Fig 4 B/C plotted values from Data S1A (or digitize the panels); place beside Fish 1990's pectoral allometry; compute the correspondence with a stated tolerance.

rows.why: They reach the identical conclusion independently: the numbers live only in the figures. They also hold a route we do not, namely the full text as a NOAA repository PDF (https://repository.library.noaa.gov/view/noaa/62581/noaa_62581_DS1.pdf, 47 pp, declared content_sha256 78cf3c283c0adc0dfe7ae85638e47ee494ef062c271df3392fd072834a352ee3) and the name of the supplement that holds the plotted values, Data S1A. That is a lead for closing our own figure-only gap.

our_claim.locator: panels[3] (panel D) genotype.description and genotype.level='hypothesis'; flier-genome.md line 22
our_claim.statement: Transfer of the lat4a x kcnh2a result to flying fishes is HYPOTHESIS ONLY: no flying-fish gene has ever been manipulated, the two conceivable routes (reverting lat4a F326L; reverting the kcnh2a regulatory state) are untested in any organism, and the one double mutant that changes fin proportion redistributes size between fins rather than scaling one fin up.
our_claim.our_evidence_grade: hypothesis

their_record.title: Hypothesis (proposed, not evidence): the zebrafish lat4a x kcnh2a fin-proportion result may carry over to flying fishes
their_record.quoted_text: payload.origin = 'hypothesis'. Statement: 'Daane et al. propose that bioelectric cues and amino-acid transport also shape relative fin size in flying fishes. Here that is a hypothesis that needs, at minimum, the paper's gene identifiers, expression of both genes in flying-fish fin tissue and a test in a flying fish or a closer proxy.' Limitations: 'No flying-fish expression or perturbation data was fetched.' / 'The mirrorwing annotation has no gene model whose best hit is KCNH2 (annotation-level only).'

their_record.title: Genome-wide signatures across 35 beloniform species associate K+/amino-acid-transport loci with increased paired-fin size (Daane et al. 2021)
their_record.quoted_text: This is an ASSOCIATION (genomic signatures), not a functional test in any flying fish. ... Limitations: 'Association only; no functional manipulation in a flying fish.' / 'Links to aerial gliding are the authors' framing; no flight mechanism is demonstrated by the genomics.' / 'Distinct from the zebrafish functional claim [[claim:daane2021-zebrafish-finproportion-phenocopy]]; no transfer between the two is asserted here.'

their_record.title: Determine whether the zebrafish lat4a/kcnh2a fin-proportion mechanism is present and active in an exocoetid
their_record.quoted_text: No functional test exists in any exocoetid; no transfer is asserted. ... No exocoetid fin transcriptomics/functional dataset located (bounded search 2026-10-31). One scaffold genome GCA_018398805.1; SRA 53 records. ... Falsifier: 'Only phylogenomic association is obtainable and no in-exocoetid expression or functional evidence exists; the transfer then remains explicitly unestablished.'

their_record.title: No causal_intervention data fetched: the lat4a x kcnh2a double-mutant phenocopy is a claim read at abstract level only
their_record.quoted_text: The only causal evidence for the fin-proportion story is the paper's zebrafish mutant experiments. The paper is not open access; no figure, genotype table or measurement was read. ZFIN has no phenotype row for kcnh2a.

their_record.title: Documentary registration: Daane, J. M. et al. (2021). Curr. Biol. PMC9172250: lat4a x kcnh2a interaction phenocopying flying-fish fin proportion in zebrafish; genome-wide signatures across 35 species.
their_record.quoted_text: upstream_source_register.caveats[0]: 'Cross-organism transfer: this does not establish that enlarging a halfbeak's fins is experimentally grounded. It is an unestablished transfer hypothesis.'

rows.why: This is the strongest independent corroboration in the whole cross-check. Four separate records, from two different issuers and three different retrieval routes (Europe PMC abstract, NOAA full-text PDF, a local repository source register), all keep the transfer at hypothesis level; one of them types it that way in the schema itself (payload.origin = 'hypothesis'), and the Daane documentary registration calls it in terms 'an unestablished transfer hypothesis'. We searched their graph for any record asserting the transfer as established and found none. Their Problem also names the specific untried next step we do not have: search the 53 exocoetid SRA records for paired-fin lat4a/kcnh2a expression.

our_claim.locator: lines 31-39, '2026-10-31 - gja5a kept out of the fin-length chain'
our_claim.statement: The gja5a-to-fin-length link offered earlier from Daane 2021 was RETRACTED: the fin-length connexin in zebrafish is gja1b (cx43, the short fin locus), gja5a has no ZFIN fin expression or phenotype record, and Daane 2021's own text puts cx43 under constrained, not accelerated, evolution along the flying-fish branch. The gja5a substitution stays in the map's fin_size block as the paper's own data and is kept out of any causal chain.
our_claim.our_evidence_grade: n/a (retraction)

rows.why: NO CONFLICT TO RAISE. frontier_search for 'gja5a' returned 0 results. 'gja' returned 5 results, none about a connexin (lexical noise matching Darwin, Wolfram and Thompson claim titles). 'cx43' returned 2 results, both bare codex-03 Problem titles ('Zebrafish fin ray joint patterning', 'Fin growth positional integration') containing no connexin assertion. 'connexin' returned 7 results, none naming a connexin gene or a fin-length link. 'short fin' returned 17 results, all either their printable-form studies or the flying-fish source registrations. So nothing in their graph asserts the link we retracted. Their graph also lacks gja1b/cx43 entirely, so our positive replacement link (gja1b with Seaver 2025) is unmatched as well.

our_claim.locator: map.json line 1604 (fin_size.verified_leads[2].symbol_check); README.md lines 69-72; HANDOVER.md lines 66-67
our_claim.statement: Our map.json asserts that lat4a = ZFIN slc43a2a is 'settled on two records' (human SLC43A2 aliased LAT4 in NCBI Gene 124935, plus ZFIN's curation of the paper's fin-length phenotypes onto slc43a2a allele dmh26). Our own HANDOVER.md line 67 contradicts this: 'NOT verified: lat4a = ZFIN slc43a2a. The aliases check found no rows ... the symbol equivalence is unproven. The map's symbol_check text overstates it. Fix that or drop it.'
our_claim.our_verdict: internally inconsistent: map.json says settled, HANDOVER says unproven
our_claim.our_evidence_grade: inference from nomenclature plus a curator's choice, not a sourced identity

their_record.title: UNRESOLVED: which ZFIN gene is the 'lat4a' of Daane et al. 2021?
their_record.quoted_text: The abstract calls lat4a 'an L-type amino acid transporter'. It is not a ZFIN symbol or alias, and gets 0 hits in NCBI Gene and UniProt. slc43a2a and slc43a2b are candidates by name (UniProt names the slc43a2b product 'Large neutral amino acids transporter small subunit 4'); neither is confirmed.

their_record.title: Source assertion: a lat4a x kcnh2a interaction in zebrafish phenocopies flying-fish fin proportions
their_record.quoted_text: Limitation: "'lat4a' is not a current ZFIN symbol (see gx-problem-lat4a-identity)."

rows.why: A genuine conflict on the same question from overlapping sources, and they are probably right. Both sides consulted ZFIN and NCBI Gene; they report 'lat4a' as neither a ZFIN symbol nor an alias, with 0 hits in NCBI Gene and UniProt, and they name slc43a2b as a second candidate our map never considers. Our 'settled' rests on an indirect chain (a human alias plus a ZFIN curator's attachment of the paper's phenotypes to slc43a2a), which is an inference, not an identity. Our own HANDOVER.md already flags the overstatement, so the real disagreement is between two of our files, with the collaborator on the side of our HANDOVER. Recommended change: downgrade map.json's symbol_check to 'candidate: slc43a2a or slc43a2b, unresolved', and cite their record as concurring. Note this does not touch the kcnh2a half of the chain.

our_claim.statement: PROPOSED (textbook limb signalling): The tetrapod AER/mesenchyme feedback loop runs on Fgf AND Wnt signals in both directions in the zebrafish pectoral fin. || OUR FINDING: The Fgf arms are supported in zebrafish but the Wnt arm is explicitly NOT established there. Leerberg 2019, full text: 'In chick and mouse, this induction appears to be mediated by WNT signaling (; ); however, this has yet to be established in zebrafish.'
our_claim.our_evidence_grade: refutation carried by a verbatim quote from a fetched full text or abstract

rows.why: No record in their graph bears on this refutation (the Wnt arm of the AER loop). The searches that would have surfaced one returned nothing relevant: 'apical ectodermal ridge Fgf Wnt' 0 results, 'sonic hedgehog zebrafish fin' 0, 'wnt10a median fin fold' 0, 'HGF MET muscle precursor' 0, 'hhip' 0, 'prdm1a' 0. 'refuted' returned 43 results and every one is an import of DELPHI's own claim-tests (delphi-claim-test--darwin1859-*, --thompson1917-*, --wolfram2002-*), none about fin signalling. The nearest adjacent thing they hold is one unrelated methodological Problem, delphi-frontier/Problem/zebrafish-mutant-morphant-discrepancy-attribution@1b38f9eb6bd106b9250eb5fdf968dfc15da0a351b06c8dc3f547b3b323742346 (codex-03, proposed), which asks how to attribute mutant/morphant discrepancies in general and makes no claim about any of these six legs. All six refutations are therefore unmatched, and they are among the most useful things we could hand over.

our_claim.statement: 42 gene-to-phenotype chains in the pectoral fin, graded by weakest link: 29 chains whose weakest link is necessity or better, 42 genes with at least one link at necessity or better, 38 with at least one mechanism link, 38 complete four-step chains, 122 distinct publications, 295 logged fetches. All proxy-species, almost all zebrafish.
our_claim.our_evidence_grade: per-link grades: mechanism / sufficiency / necessity / association / hypothesis

rows.why: Their graph holds no graded gene-to-phenotype chain for any fin gene. 'causal chain' returned 10 results, all of them bioelectric simulation scenarios (sim-bioelectric-claim-atlas / -baseline / -disconnected / -no_stimulus / -sodium_reduced, a membrane-potential sweep over sodium scale and gap conductance), not causal chains in our sense. Their only chain-like structure is the Problem.dependencies edge set between source claims, which carries no evidence grade. Their catalogue also reports origin_declared 'unknown' for 1214 of 1287 claims, so most of their store has no declared epistemic origin at all.

our_claim.statement: Requirement 1 needs pectoral lifting area about 3.9x the real fish's and span about 2.5x at a similar aspect ratio; the route is PARTIAL. The largest measured increase from any single manipulation is hhip loss of function at +65% of wild-type pectoral fin area (larval, 72 hpf) against the +290% required, no manipulation anywhere was measured as a span or an aspect ratio, and pectoral fin LENGTH has no calibrated route at all.
our_claim.our_verdict: partial; no route reaches the required magnitude
our_claim.our_evidence_grade: necessity (hhip effect size), with pleiotropy on 12 blueprint nodes

their_record.title: Fixed-launch glide ranges of three wing geometries in a point-mass model with an assumed polar
their_record.quoted_text: In the producer's point-mass glide model with the assumed polar above, released at 12.0 m/s from 1.0 m, the computed nominal ranges are: baseline (Fish Cypselurus fit, 0.05 kg): nominal range 25.14 m, MC q10/q50/q90 12.9/21.6/26.4 m; area x1.3: nominal range 29.45 m, MC q10/q50/q90 23.2/26.0/28.9 m; area x1.3, AR x1.2: nominal range 29.41 m, MC q10/q50/q90 23.2/27.0/30.3 m. ... Limitation: 'Producer states it does not establish: which geometry is better: ranking flips with release speed'

their_record.title: Declared-constraint check for printable form N3-area-x1.3-ar-x1.2: Comparison N3: wing area x1.3, aspect ratio x1.2
their_record.quoted_text: For the declared constraint set of design N3-area-x1.3-ar-x1.2 (N1 with wing area x1.3 and whole-wing b^2/S x1.2 ...), the producer's z3 solver reports feasible; witness S=370439/50000000, V=16, b=264397/1000000, m=1/20. ... Limitation: 'Constraint satisfaction on a declared constraint set says nothing about whether the form flies or is biologically viable.'

rows.why: A scope difference, not a conflict. We ask what a GENETIC manipulation can deliver and answer 1.65x area at best with span and aspect ratio never measured; they ask what a geometric change buys AERODYNAMICALLY (area x1.3 lifts their modelled glide range from 25.14 m to 29.45 m, and adding aspect ratio x1.2 adds nothing: 29.41 m) and whether such a shape satisfies a declared constraint set. Neither side evaluates the other's quantity, so the rows are complementary rather than confirming. Two of their own caveats limit how far their numbers can be used: the polar is a design assumption (C_Lmax 1.2, C_D0 0.06, e 0.8), not a measured fish polar, and the ranking among geometries flips with release speed.

our_claim.statement: Requirement 2 (an aerobic pectoral flight muscle at about 16% of body mass): PARTIAL for 'more muscle', NONE for the requirement as stated. Myostatin loss of function gives +16% to +41% skeletal muscle across seven teleost species, but every result is an increment on axial/trunk muscle rather than an allocation, no fetched source reports pectoral fin muscle as a fraction of body mass in any fish, the effect is predominantly hyperplastic (medaka: fibre number doubled with gross muscle mass unaltered), and the side effects (short body, fewer/shorter vertebrae, intramuscular fat) hit exactly the support a flight muscle would need.
our_claim.our_evidence_grade: necessity to mechanism per species; the mass-fraction requirement has no route

rows.why: Searches 'mstn' 0 results, 'myostatin' 0, 'myostatin muscle mass' 0. 'muscle' returned 28 results, none about muscle-mass genetics; the only muscle-adjacent record is the import of our own thompson1917-ch02-06 claim (muscle power grows as L^3). The whole of our requirement-2 analysis, including the explicit warning that the two senses of '16%' are different quantities, is unmatched.

our_claim.statement: Requirement 3 (oxygen delivery about 5x the bat range per kilogram): route NONE. Every fetched genetic result on fish globins runs downward (icefish haemoglobin cluster loss by transposable-element-mediated deletion, noodlefish myoglobin loss, notothenioid reduction to one low-affinity isoform, icefish candidate FAAP20 associated with LOW haematocrit); the two positive cardiac routes are compensatory or pathological; and the highest fetched fish maximum oxygen uptake is 781.31 +/- 16.50 mg O2 per kg per hour with a maximum cardiac output of 69.12 +/- 2.39 ml/min/kg in schoolmaster snapper, nowhere near the requirement.
our_claim.our_evidence_grade: association to mechanism per result; every direction negative for the requirement

rows.why: 'aerobic' returned 0 results in the entire store. 'oxygen' returned 3 results, all unrelated codex-03 Problems (zebrafish regeneration enhancer activation, mammalian body size control, tracheal terminal cell branch placement and scaling). 'cardiac output arterial oxygen content' returned 0. Their graph contains no oxygen-transport physiology at all, so neither our negative result nor the Lean elimination that depends on it has any counterpart there.

our_claim.statement: Requirement 4 (a respiratory surface that works in air): route PARTIAL. their_record.title: Darwin's flying-fish passage is an explicit 'imaginary illustration' / conceivability argument (Origin ch. VI)
their_record.quoted_text: In On the Origin of Species (ch. VI; 1st ed. 1859 p.182 through 6th ed. 1872 p.140) Darwin calls flying fish 'our imaginary illustration' and argues only subjunctively that flying fish might, if selection had run that way, have been modified into winged animals. It is a conceivability argument against an objection, not a claim that flying fish are becoming flyers. ... Limitations: "Darwin never writes 'Exocoetus' in the 1859/1860/1872 editions (independent grep)." / 'Not a prediction of an inevitable evolutionary path and not a claim of actual precursor species.' / "'Fluttering fins' does not match the modern gliding mechanism."

rows.why: A framing correction we should adopt. They read the Darwin Online variorum across all six British editions and establish that the passage is an explicit conceivability argument rather than a prediction, that Darwin never names Exocoetus, and that his 'fluttering fins' is a 19th-century conjecture at odds with the modern passive-gliding mechanism. That last point is the same correction our own prior-art report makes when it insists on 'fin enlargement for gliding' rather than 'fin-to-wing', so the two reinforce each other on how the project should describe its premise.

their_record.title: Source assertion: mirrorwing flyingfish draft genome of 1.04 Gb with 23,611 predicted protein-coding genes
their_record.quoted_text: Xu et al. (first author Xu P; author list from Europe PMC) state a 1.04 Gb assembly (contig N50 992.83 kb, scaffold N50 1,152.47 kb), 23,611 predicted protein-coding genes (99.5% functionally annotated), BUSCO completeness 94.2% (genome) and 95.7% (gene set, actinopterygii_odb9 4,584), with the assembly under BioProject PRJNA714815 and the annotation in figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.14600634.v1. [species: Hirundichthys speculiger; open access, full-text, CC BY, PMC8294118]

their_record.title: Annotation-derived: 29 mirrorwing flyingfish gene models have a best SwissProt hit in the fin / mechanosensation gene set
their_record.quoted_text: In the authors' annotation (23,611 gene models), 29 models whose inferred gene-model id passed a per-gene protein-length check and whose best-hit paralog is compatible with the set have a best SwissProt BLASTP hit named for one of the set's genes: FGF10, FGF20, KCNJ13, LEF1, PIEZO1, PIEZO2, PKD2, PPP3CA, RUNX2, SHH, SLC43A2, SP7, TBX5, TMC2, WNT5B. ... Each is a best-hit similarity (identity 49.3 to 92.5%), not an orthology call, and paralogs (a/b) are not resolved. Limitations: 'No synteny or reciprocal-best-hit check.' / 'Absence of a symbol among best hits is not absence from the genome.'

their_record.title: Annotation-derived: FGF24, HOXD13, KCNH2, MSX1 are not best SwissProt hits of any mirrorwing gene model
their_record.quoted_text: No mirrorwing gene model has a best SwissProt hit named FGF24, HOXD13, KCNH2, MSX1. 6 hits to KCNH2 exist (on 4 distinct gene models) but those models' best hits are other genes (for example KCNH7); HOXD13 and FGF24 have no hit at all in the table. This describes this annotation of one assembly, not the genome. ... Relevant because kcnh2a is half of the Daane fin-proportion story; it is NOT evidence that kcnh2 is missing from the species.

their_record.title: Is there a kcnh2 gene in the mirrorwing genome that the annotation did not name as such?
their_record.quoted_text: Do kcnh2, hoxd13 and msx1 sequences exist in the assembly, and are they annotated under other names? ... No gene model has KCNH2 as its best SwissProt hit; KCNH7 is the best hit for the nearest queries. ... Assembly sequence (311 MB figshare file) not downloaded.

rows.why: The most actionable lead they hold. They have actually worked a flying-fish genome: Hirundichthys speculiger (mirrorwing), PMC8294118 under CC BY, BioProject PRJNA714815, annotation at figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.14600634.v1 (CC BY 4.0, declared md5 d283a670a8d3a2cb0bdda585df0020ba), from which they derive 29 fin-gene best hits including SLC43A2, the very family our lat4a identity question turns on, plus the negative result that no gene model has KCNH2 as a best hit. That is a real route into the exocoetid side of our causal chains, which we currently mark as having no molecular data. Carry their caveats: best hits are not orthology calls, a/b paralogs are unresolved, the gene-model id mapping is an inference checked only by protein length (90.1% agreement against 4.1% and 4.3% for one-gene shifts), and a missing best hit can mean fragmented annotation or divergent sequence rather than a missing gene. Their own open Problem is the obvious joint task: search the assembly sequence for an unnamed kcnh2.

our_claim.statement: We record that there is no measurement of membrane potential or intracellular K+/Ca2+ in a kcnh2a-expressing fin cell, that the sufficiency experiment used HUMAN KCNH2 rather than zebrafish kcnh2a, and that no cell type is resolved for lat4a in the fin (no transplantation, no clonal mosaic, no cell-type driver).
our_claim.our_evidence_grade: n/a

their_record.title: Curated database content: ZFIN holds 19 wildtype expression annotations for kcnh2a, all by RT-PCR
their_record.quoted_text: ZFIN's wildtype-expression table has 19 rows for kcnh2a (zebrafish): 11 adult tissue rows including 'fin' and 'regenerating fin' (publication ZDB-PUB-210918-31) and 8 whole-organism rows across embryonic and larval stages. Assay: Reverse transcription PCR only; no in situ annotation. Limitations: 'Absent annotations mean not curated, not not expressed.' / 'RT-PCR on whole tissue does not localise expression to cell types.'

their_record.title: Expression correlation (weak): the genes most correlated with kcnh2a across all Daniocell cells have |r| at most 0.082
their_record.quoted_text: On the Daniocell kcnh2a all-cells page the top positive correlation is kcnmb2 (r = 0.082) and the listed correlations are all small; the page lists 35 positive and 35 negative partners. ... It shows neither interaction nor regulation nor function.

rows.why: Two specific negatives we lack that sharpen our own gap statement. kcnh2a's ZFIN expression evidence is RT-PCR only, so it cannot localise to a cell type, which is exactly the cell-type resolution our chains report as missing; and single-cell co-expression in Daniocell gives kcnh2a no partner above |r| = 0.082. Both strengthen rather than weaken our position that the kcnh2a arm of the chain is thin, and both are citable as independent database reads.

our_claim.statement: Our structural theorems cannot be evaluated because we have no breaking stress for fin-ray or bone material in Exocoetidae and no load-bearing cross-sections at two sizes.
our_claim.our_evidence_grade: n/a

their_record.title: Declared-load critical bending stiffness of a single clamped-free ray (linear small-deformation surrogate)
their_record.quoted_text: For the producer's declared request ..., in a linear static Euler-Bernoulli cantilever with a uniform line load from a declared lift-pressure proxy, the bending stiffness below which the declared small-deformation limits are exceeded is EI_crit = 1323/2048000 N m^2 (binding limit: tip_over_L). Decision rule stated by the producer: 'If measured EI >= EI_crit_Nm2 the declared load stays inside the small-deformation limit for this geometry; if EI < EI_crit_Nm2 the linear model is invalid at the declared load and a large-deformation model (or a lower load) is required.' Limitations: 'EI is an ASSUMED log-spaced range (1/1000000 to 1 N m^2), not a measurement of any fin ray.' / 'DECLARED ILLUSTRATION: not produced by the dx-guilds solver; numbers are test values, not a design claim.'

rows.why: A method lead, not evidence. Their record does not supply the fin-ray material data our structural theorems need either (EI is an assumed sweep and the producer labels the whole thing a declared illustration with test values), but the Euler-Bernoulli cantilever surrogate and its explicit decision rule give us a template to instantiate the moment a measured EI appears, which would turn two of our 'cannot-evaluate' rows into evaluable ones.
